verdict_rationale: The windowed recall-at-5%-FPR scorer is the metric the prompt states, it is deterministic, and the 3x real-time gate is measured on a trusted server-side clock and projected faithfully in the self-check. But the task's defining constraint, causality, is never tested by the grader. The held-out set is 30 conversations of a public, findable dev release that agents are not told to avoid by name. With the high floor, noise is about 4 points.
floor: 0 = raw recall 0.655 of a training-free two-channel silence heuristic: own-channel silence ramp plus partner speech since offset (tests/task/task.yaml:46-48; tests/task/baselines/offline_baselines.py). The split it was measured on and the scorer version (dated 2026-09-26) are not stated. The heuristic is not shipped to agents in /task. It is a sensible floor and a high one: the 1 s late window lets partner-onset detection alone recover most turn ends. 9 trials that passed review still scored 0 (below the heuristic or a gate failure).
ceiling: 1.0 = perfect recall, not measured. It is unreachable in practice: there is consensus-label noise, a 5% FPR budget on about 819 pauses, and positive windows with no scoreable frame count as misses (turn_taking.py:87). The best observed raw recall is 0.913 (1390/1523), or 74.7 points. The ceiling does not bind; about 25 points at the top are probably unattainable.
usable_range: observed 0-74.7 of 0-100; 21 of 57 trials score 0 (12 review fails, 9 passing review but at or below the heuristic or failing a gate)
feasible_at_10: yes: Opus 74.7 (the best of any wallet), Fable 65.0 and Kimi K3.1 Pro 63.6 at $10. Frozen speech encoders plus small causal heads train in hours.
budget_scaling: None or negative. Opus 74.7/68.8/55.8, Gemini 53.2/65.2/64.8, Astra 50.5/62.9/60.4. Approach choice dominates, and Astra placed well after fitting heads on the 8 shipped conversations in under an hour.
selfcheck_fidelity: Good for the speed gate. The self-check sends two public conversations close to the held-out mean length through the grader's parser and the same ServerClock, then projects the 20,455 s pass, charging the cold first request once (verifier.py:29-35, 72-110). It does not test causality, which the grader does not test either. A non-causal server passes the self-check and grading and is zeroed only by the reviewer.
judge: None in the metric. Scoring is a deterministic threshold sweep (turn_taking.py:126-150). The rule-heavy LLM review (Claude Opus 5.5) decides causality and data provenance, and the audit found it inconsistent on end-anchored windows (Fable 4dhosx failed, DeepSeek 64qbza passed).
neutrality: Favours agents that identify the benchmark. Label field names lead to TurnBench by web search. Its official training split (otoSpeech-104h) and gold code are legitimately allowed and in-distribution, and Opus $50 and DeepSeek used them. The held-out conversations are TurnBench dev ids, published on GitHub and HF (including an ungated derivative). Avoiding them requires knowing what they are, and the review fails any appearance of the ids even in an exclusion list (review.py:38-41). The 5 ms resampler tolerance exists only in the review policy (review.py:16-20). No vendor-specific judge.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture. /predict returns all-zero streams at a 0.2 s hop (solution/server.py:91-94), which gives no qualifying threshold, so recall 0 and score 0. The training-free heuristic in tests/task/baselines defines the floor and would fail the 'learned_causal_model' check. Solvability is shown by the trials, not by the repo.

issues.finding: Causality, the task's central constraint, is never checked by the grader. The server receives whole files, and only the LLM reviewer reads code for lookahead. A prefix-truncation or chunked-replay test in the grader would settle it. The audit shows the reviewer judging the same end-of-file-anchored window pattern differently in two trials.

issues.finding: The held-out set is 30 of the 38 conversations of the public TurnBench dev release, with labels, on HF gated 'auto' and as an ungated derivative. Agents are told only 'Do not use any other copy or derivative of this task's conversations', without the source. Protection rests on the reviewer, and finding the benchmark also unlocks its allowed in-distribution training split.

issues.finding: The review enforces rules that are not in the prompt or contract. Any held-out TurnBench id in a file, list or log fails the run, even in an exclusion list (this zeroed DeepSeek 61zfoj). A 5 ms anti-aliasing lookahead tolerance applies to standard resamplers only, while whole-file FFT resampling fails (this zeroed Muse twice).

issues.finding: The sample is small and clustered: 1,523 positive and 819 pause windows from 30 conversations. One positive is worth 0.19 points. The binomial SE alone is about 2.4 points; with threshold noise from about 41 allowed false positives and conversation-level correlation it is about 4 points.

issues.finding: The floor provenance does not give the split or the scorer revision, and the 'shipped' heuristic is not in /task for agents. Because the 1 s late window credits detection after the partner starts talking, a trivial heuristic gets 65.5% recall. Clipping then puts below-heuristic trained models (up to 9 review-passing trials) at the same 0 as failures.

issues.finding: The title promises replies 'promptly without interrupting', but latency within the 1 s late window is not scored, only reported. The upstream reference uses a 3 s window; this task narrows it to 1 s, but any detection up to 1 s late counts fully.

issues.finding: A window with no scoreable frames (fully inside a disputed region) gets statistic 0. Such positive windows stay in the recall denominator and can never fire, which lowers the reachable ceiling. Such pause windows can never be false positives. The effect is small and the same for every submission.
